62298.subject: Technical Drawing
62298.question_text: Construct a perpendicular bisector to a line segment AB of length 60 mm using only a compass and a straightedge. Label all construction lines and points clearly.
62298.explanation:
1. Draw line segment AB = 60 mm.
2. With A as center, draw an arc with radius greater than half of AB.
3. With B as center, draw another arc of the same radius to intersect the first arc at points C and D.
4. Draw a straight line through C and D. This line is the perpendicular bisector of AB.
5. Label the intersection of the bisector with AB as point M, the midpoint of AB.

62299.subject: Technical Drawing
62299.question_text: Construct a regular hexagon with each side measuring 30 mm, using only a compass and a straightedge. Show all construction lines.
62299.explanation:
1. Draw a circle with radius 30 mm.
2. Mark a point A on the circumference.
3. Using the same radius, step off points B, C, D, E, and F on the circumference.
4. Join points A, B, C, D, E, and F to form the regular hexagon.
5. Label all vertices and construction lines.

62300.subject: Technical Drawing
62300.question_text: Construct a tangent to a circle of radius 25 mm from an external point P, 50 mm from the center O of the circle. Show all construction lines.
62300.explanation:
1. Draw the circle with center O and radius 25 mm.
2. Mark point P 50 mm from O.
3. Draw line OP.
4. Construct the perpendicular bisector of OP to find its midpoint M.
5. With M as center and radius OM, draw a semicircle to intersect the original circle at points T and T'.
6. Draw lines PT and PT'. These are the required tangents.
7. Label all points and construction lines.

62301.subject: Technical Drawing
62301.question_text: Draw the front, top, and right-side views of the given object in first-angle orthographic projection. The object is a rectangular block 50 mm × 30 mm × 20 mm with a semicircular slot of radius 10 mm cut into the top face along the 50 mm length. Show all hidden details.
62301.explanation:
1. Draw the front view: 50 mm (length) × 20 mm (height) rectangle with a semicircle of radius 10 mm at the top.
2. Draw the top view: 50 mm × 30 mm rectangle with a hidden semicircle (dashed line) of radius 10 mm.
3. Draw the right-side view: 30 mm (width) × 20 mm (height) rectangle with a hidden semicircle (dashed line) of radius 10 mm.
4. Ensure all hidden lines are dashed and visible lines are continuous.
5. Label all views and dimensions.

62302.subject: Technical Drawing
62302.question_text: Given the front and top views of an object in first-angle projection, draw the right-side view. The front view shows a rectangle 40 mm × 25 mm with a circular hole of diameter 15 mm centered on the vertical axis. The top view shows a rectangle 40 mm × 30 mm with a hidden circular hole (dashed line).
62302.explanation:
1. Analyze the front and top views to determine the depth (30 mm) and height (25 mm).
2. Draw the right-side view: 30 mm (width) × 25 mm (height) rectangle.
3. Add the circular hole of diameter 15 mm centered vertically and horizontally.
4. Ensure the hole is shown as a hidden line (dashed) if not visible.
5. Label all views and dimensions.

62303.subject: Technical Drawing
62303.question_text: Draw a full sectional front view of the given object, which is a hollow cylinder of external diameter 50 mm, internal diameter 30 mm, and height 40 mm, cut by a vertical plane through its axis. Show the section hatching.
62303.explanation:
1. Draw the front view as a rectangle 50 mm (width) × 40 mm (height).
2. Draw the internal diameter as a dashed line (30 mm) in the unsectioned view.
3. For the sectional view, draw the outer and inner rectangles.
4. Add section hatching (45° lines) to the solid material between the outer and inner diameters.
5. Label the view and dimensions.

62304.subject: Technical Drawing
62304.question_text: Draw an isometric view of a rectangular block 60 mm × 40 mm × 30 mm with a circular hole of diameter 20 mm drilled through the center of the top face. Show all hidden details.
62304.explanation:
1. Draw the isometric axes at 30° to the horizontal.
2. Construct the isometric box: 60 mm (length), 40 mm (width), and 30 mm (height).
3. On the top face, draw an ellipse (isometric circle) of diameter 20 mm centered.
4. Show the hole as a hidden ellipse (dashed) on the bottom face.
5. Label all dimensions and ensure proper isometric scaling.

62305.subject: Technical Drawing
62305.question_text: Develop the lateral surface of a right circular cone with base diameter 50 mm and slant height 60 mm. Show all construction lines.
62305.explanation:
1. Calculate the circumference of the base: $C = \pi imes 50 = 157$ mm.
2. Draw a sector of a circle with radius 60 mm (slant height) and arc length 157 mm.
3. The angle of the sector is calculated as $ heta = rac{157}{60} imes rac{180}{\pi} \approx 150°$.
4. Draw the sector with the calculated angle and radius.
5. Label the development and construction lines.

62306.subject: Technical Drawing
62306.question_text: Draw the line of intersection between a vertical cylinder of diameter 40 mm and a horizontal cylinder of diameter 30 mm, both intersecting at right angles. Show the front and top views.
62306.explanation:
1. Draw the front view: vertical cylinder as a rectangle 40 mm × height, horizontal cylinder as a circle 30 mm diameter.
2. Draw the top view: vertical cylinder as a circle 40 mm diameter, horizontal cylinder as a rectangle 30 mm × length.
3. Project points of intersection from the top view to the front view.
4. Draw the intersection curve in the front view as a smooth curve connecting the projected points.
5. Label all views and construction lines.

62307.subject: Technical Drawing
62307.question_text: Dimension the following orthographic views of a simple bracket: front view (rectangle 50 mm × 30 mm with a 10 mm diameter hole centered 15 mm from the top edge) and top view (rectangle 50 mm × 20 mm with the same hole). Apply standard dimensioning conventions.
62307.explanation:
1. In the front view:
- Dimension the overall height (30 mm) and width (50 mm).
- Dimension the hole diameter (10 mm) with a leader line.
- Dimension the vertical position of the hole (15 mm from the top edge).
2. In the top view:
- Dimension the overall width (50 mm) and depth (20 mm).
- Dimension the hole diameter (10 mm) if not already shown in the front view.
3. Ensure dimensions are placed outside the views, with no redundant dimensions.
4. Use standard dimensioning symbols (e.g., Ø for diameter).
